family.tagline: Different shifts, one family plan, and dinner at the table.
family.story: Linh is a nurse on rotating shifts and Rory teaches primary school. Their daughter Mai is six, and dinner is the one fixed point in the week. Recipes from three grandparents, on two continents, and the family plan sit on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Juno
companion.job: Turns the family's week of messages into a shift and dinner plan.
companion.limits: Proposes a plan. Linh edits and confirms it.

companion.name: Angus
companion.job: Opens KitchenOwl in its own browser and types in the recipes Rory points to.
companion.limits: Saves a copy. Rory edits the recipe.

popup.title: A parcel between shifts
popup.body: The parcel arrives on a Tuesday morning, between Linh's shifts. Rory carries it into the library lounge and clears the bottom shelf.

popup.title: Linh lays it all out
popup.body: Linh lays out the contents: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Mai presses the button
popup.body: Rory plugs in the cable and Mai presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it between shifts
popup.body: Linh joins the Core's own network from her phone. She picks the home network and types its password.

popup.title: Pick the agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Linh picks Hermes and Rory picks OpenClaw. They add Yuvomi, KitchenOwl and VaultWarden, then walk away to start dinner.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Juno says hello
popup.body: Linh sends the first message to Juno, the agent she named. Juno answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: linh
say.text: Hello, Linh. Juno here. What does the week look like?

beats.capability: Stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: A father's cassettes, playing again
popup.body: Rory saved his father's old cassettes as audio files. On Sunday, Navidrome plays them from the loveseat, and Mai asks for the song about the frog.

beats.capability: A whiteboard with a hand-drawn look

popup.title: Monday's lesson, sketched
popup.body: Rory sketches Monday's lesson on an Excalidraw whiteboard by the bookshelves. He prints the board for the class, and the original stays on the Core.

beats.capability: Block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: The router asks Pi-hole first
popup.body: Rory sets the router to ask Pi-hole first. It blocks ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level for every device in the house.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Juno drafts the week
popup.body: On Sunday evening, Linh sends Juno the week's messages. Juno drafts a plan of shifts and dinners. Linh edits it in Yuvomi.

say.speaker: linh
say.text: Plan drafted. Please edit before you confirm.

beats.capability: A family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals, notes, contacts and budget in one

popup.title: Who is cooking tonight?
popup.body: Whoever gets home first opens Yuvomi on the fridge door. Tonight's dinner, who is cooking and who is on shift are all on one page.

beats.capability: A small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: One calendar, two timetables
popup.body: Linh's shifts and Rory's school terms share one calendar in Baikal. It runs on the Core and syncs to both phones over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: A shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: Angus keeps the old recipes
popup.body: Rory reads out the recipe Linh's grandmother used to make. Angus opens KitchenOwl in its own browser and types it in. Rory corrects the quantities.

say.speaker: rory
say.text: Recipe saved. Please check the quantities.

beats.capability: Store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Logins, moved into one vault
popup.body: At the dining table, Rory moves the family's logins into VaultWarden. It works with the Bitwarden apps, and the vault lives on the Core.

beats.capability: Archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: Every slip and warranty, kept
popup.body: Linh scans permission slips, warranties and the dishwasher manual into Papra. Months later, one search finds the right page.

beats.capability: Track accounts, budgets, bills and savings goals, with rules that sort your transactions

popup.title: Last month's statement, sorted
popup.body: Linh imports last month's bank statement as a CSV file into Firefly III. Its rules sort each line into a category.

beats.capability: Turn a folder of photos and videos into a private feed with albums and a timeline

popup.title: A year of Mai's drawings
popup.body: On Sunday, Rory photographs Mai's school drawings. Foldergram turns the folder into an album feed, so her year in pictures has a timeline.

beats.capability: Read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: A picture book, read aloud
popup.body: Linh opens a picture book in Koodo Reader and turns on text-to-speech. Mai follows along with her finger under each line.

beats.capability: Assign and track household chores and recurring tasks, with NFC tag completion

popup.title: Mai's chore has a tag
popup.body: Donetick lists the family's chores, and Mai's is watering the herbs. A tag on the pot lets her mark it done.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: The landing lights keep her hours
popup.body: After a night shift, Linh sleeps while a Home Assistant schedule keeps the landing lights low. It runs on the Core.

beats.capability: Track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Coriander for the soup
popup.body: Rory and Mai plant coriander for Linh's grandmother's soup. HortusFox keeps the planting date, a watering log and a picture for each pot.

beats.capability: Send files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi

popup.title: Sunday dinner, sent across the table
popup.body: Rory sends the photos of Sunday dinner to Linh's laptop with PairDrop, over the home Wi-Fi. Mai insists on the one with her thumb in it.

beats.capability: Plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: Saturday's ride, mapped
popup.body: Rory plans a Saturday bike ride with Mai in Wanderer. He loads a GPX file, and the route is saved on the Core.

popup.title: Three timetables, one plan
popup.body: Two shifts, a school day and a six-year-old. The Tran-McAllister household keeps its week on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your family's week, your recipes and your logins can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one grandmother's recipe in KitchenOwl.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
Cast gave Angus a job built on Mealie. Mealie has no QA screenshot and reviewed.json is empty, so only the job text changed, to KitchenOwl. Name, runtime, voice and limits are as cast.
Shift work is told as a scheduling story only. No health claim; no workplace is named. Linh is a nurse (cast work); the text never says where.
Yuvomi appears in ftue-pick, kitchen-plan (named inside the Hermes beat) and kitchen-board. Juno only drafts; Linh edits and confirms in Yuvomi herself (Hermes cannot act on a ui-only app).
Firefly III (dining-statement): bank sync is an outside service (catalog caveat), so the text says a CSV file. Bookkeeping only, no financial advice.
Home Assistant (bedroom-lights): the lights are devices on the home network. No energy, sleep or health claim; the schedule is Linh's.
Donetick's notifications use Telegram or Pushover (catalog caveat); the text mentions only an NFC tag on a pot, which the listing names. Pi-hole is DNS-level blocking, not parental control.
Town Tallowfield and street Wattlebird Crescent are invented and still need the human map check. Grandparents are named only as "Linh's grandmother" and "Rory's father".
